statement: Let N = m * n and s = k mod N (the remainder in 0 <= s < N). The function returns a result r such that len(r) = m, len(r[i]) = n for every 0 <= i < m, and for every p with 0 <= p < N, writing q = (p + s) mod N, we have r[q / n][q % n] = grid[p / n][p % n]. Here p / n and p % n denote row-major division and remainder.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). The input satisfies: 1 <= m <= 50; let n = len(grid[0]) (well-defined since m >= 1); 1 <= n <= 50; for every i with 0 <= i < m, len(grid[i]) = n; for every i with 0 <= i < m and every j with 0 <= j < n, -1000 <= grid[i][j] <= 1000; and 0 <= k <= 100.
